title: A Causal Framework for Discovering and Removing Direct and Indirect Discrimination
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of discovering both direct and indirect discrimination from the historical data, and removing the discriminatory effects before the data is used for predictive analysis (e.g., building classifiers). The main drawback of existing methods is that they cannot distinguish the part of influence that is really caused by discrimination from all correlated influences. In our approach, we make use of the causal network to capture the causal structure of the data. Then we model direct and indirect discrimination as the path-specific effects, which accurately identify the two types of discrimination as the causal effects transmitted along different paths in the network. Based on that, we propose an effective algorithm for discovering direct and indirect discrimination, as well as an algorithm for precisely removing both types of discrimination while retaining good data utility. Experiments using the real dataset show the effectiveness of our approaches.

claims.text: On the Adult dataset, the direct path-specific effect of sex on income (SE_πd) is measured as 0.025.
On the Adult dataset, the indirect path-specific effect of sex on income passing through marital status (SE_πi) is measured as 0.175.
On the Dutch Census 2001 dataset, the direct path-specific effect of sex on occupation (SE_πd) is measured as 0.220.
On the Dutch Census 2001 dataset, the indirect path-specific effect of sex on occupation through marital status (SE_πi) is measured as 0.001.
Applying PSE-DR to the Adult dataset reduces SE_πd to 0.013 and SE_πi to 0.049.
Applying PSE-DR to the Dutch Census dataset reduces SE_πd to 0.050 and SE_πi to 0.001.
Predictive models trained on PSE-DR modified Adult data maintain indirect discriminatory effects below 0.05 while achieving around 80.55% prediction accuracy.
Predictive models trained on data modified by Disparate Impact Removal retain significant indirect discrimination (0.167 for SVM and 0.168 for Decision Tree) in test set predictions.

limitations.text: Classic discrimination metrics like risk difference treat all difference in decisions as discrimination and fail to separate direct, indirect, and explainable effects.
Existing discrimination removal algorithms (such as DI, LMSG, and LPS) cannot ensure that predictive models built from modified data are free from discrimination.
The computational complexity of the PC algorithm for constructing causal networks grows exponentially with the number of attributes and domain sizes, requiring domain binarization.
When the recanting witness criterion is satisfied, indirect path-specific effects cannot be estimated directly from observational data alone.

methodologies.name: Path-Specific based Discrimination Discovery (PSE-DD)
methodologies.description: An algorithm that constructs a causal network from observational data and evaluates direct and indirect discrimination using path-specific causal effects.
conditions: PC algorithm with significance threshold 0.01 for causal graph construction

methodologies.name: Path-Specific Effect based Discrimination Removal (PSE-DR)
methodologies.description: A data preprocessing algorithm that modifies the conditional probability table of the decision attribute via quadratic programming to enforce discrimination bounds while preserving data utility.
